questions.q:
A box plot shows the following values for the marks in a test: minimum 12, lower quartile 18, median 25, upper quartile 29, maximum 41.
(a) Find the interquartile range. [1]
(b) What percentage of the marks are greater than 18? [1]
questions.model:
(a) IQR = 29 − 18 = 11.
(b) 18 is the lower quartile, so 75% of the marks are above it.
questions.tip: Each section of a box plot (whisker or half-box) contains 25% of the data.

questions.q:
The masses, m kg, of 60 dogs are shown in the table.

Mass (m kg)   40 < m ≤ 50   50 < m ≤ 60   60 < m ≤ 70   70 < m ≤ 80   80 < m ≤ 90
Frequency          5             12            23            14             6

(a) Work out the cumulative frequencies. [2]
(b) Write down the coordinates of the points you would plot for the first two classes on a cumulative frequency graph. [1]
ms: B1: at least three cumulative frequencies correct
(b) B1: (50, 5) and (60, 17) (plotted at upper class boundaries; allow also (40, 0))
questions.model:
(a) Cumulative frequencies: 5, 17, 40, 54, 60.
(b) Points are plotted at the upper class boundaries: (50, 5) and (60, 17). The curve starts at (40, 0).
questions.tip: Plot cumulative frequency at the upper class boundary, never at the midpoint.

questions.q:
The cumulative frequency table shows the times, t minutes, taken by 80 runners to complete a fun run.

Time (t min)          t ≤ 20   t ≤ 25   t ≤ 30   t ≤ 35   t ≤ 40   t ≤ 45
Cumulative frequency     4        15       38       61       74       80

(a) Use linear interpolation to estimate the median time. [2]
(b) Estimate the number of runners who took more than 37 minutes. [2]
questions.model:
(a) Median is the 40th value (80 ÷ 2), which lies between t = 30 (cf 38) and t = 35 (cf 61).
Median ≈ 30 + (40 − 38) ÷ 23 × 5 = 30 + 0.43 = 30.4 minutes.
(b) 13 runners finished between 35 and 40 minutes. Up to 37 minutes: 61 + 2/5 × 13 = 61 + 5.2 = 66.2.
More than 37 minutes: 80 − 66.2 = 13.8, so about 14 runners.
questions.tip: "More than" means subtract the cumulative frequency from the total.

questions.q:
A data set has minimum 15, lower quartile 34, median 41, upper quartile 46 and maximum 62.
An outlier is a value more than 1.5 × IQR below the lower quartile or above the upper quartile.
(a) Show that 15 is an outlier but 62 is not. [3]
(b) Describe the skewness of the data. Give a reason. [1]
(c) Describe how the outlier should be shown when the box plot is drawn. [1]
ms: A1: lower limit 34 − 18 = 16 and 15 < 16 so 15 is an outlier
A1: upper limit 46 + 18 = 64 and 62 < 64 so 62 is not an outlier
(b) B1: negative skew since Q₃ − Q₂ = 5 < Q₂ − Q₁ = 7 (oe)
(c) B1: marked with a cross (separate point) at 15, with the lower whisker drawn only to the smallest value that is not an outlier
questions.model:
(a) IQR = 46 − 34 = 12, and 1.5 × 12 = 18.
Lower limit = 34 − 18 = 16. 15 < 16, so 15 is an outlier.
Upper limit = 46 + 18 = 64. 62 < 64, so 62 is not an outlier.
(b) Q₃ − Q₂ = 46 − 41 = 5 and Q₂ − Q₁ = 41 − 34 = 7. Since 5 < 7, the data have negative skew.
(c) Plot 15 as a cross on its own, and draw the lower whisker only to the lowest value that is not an outlier.
questions.tip: Show both limits as numbers and compare each one with the value; "it is far away" gets no marks.

questions.q:
The marks of 120 students in a test are summarised below.

Mark (x)    0 < x ≤ 20   20 < x ≤ 40   40 < x ≤ 60   60 < x ≤ 80   80 < x ≤ 100
Frequency        6            18            42            36            18

(a) Use linear interpolation to estimate the median and the lower and upper quartiles. [4]
(b) Grade A is given to the top 10% of students. Estimate the lowest mark needed for a grade A. [2]
For a second class, the median mark was 51 and the interquartile range was 22.
(c) Compare the marks of the two groups. [2]
ms: M1: cumulative frequencies 6, 24, 66, 102, 120 and median at 60th value: 40 + (60 − 24) ÷ 42 × 20
A1: median 57.1 (awrt 57.1; allow 56–58 from a graph)
(c) B1: the first group has a higher median (57.1 v 51), so generally scored higher (ft)
(c) B1: the first group has a larger IQR (30.4 v 22), so its marks were less consistent / more spread out (ft)
questions.model:
(a) Cumulative frequencies: 6, 24, 66, 102, 120.
Median = 60th value: 40 + (60 − 24) ÷ 42 × 20 = 40 + 17.1 = 57.1.
Q₁ = 30th value: 40 + (30 − 24) ÷ 42 × 20 = 42.9.
Q₃ = 90th value: 60 + (90 − 66) ÷ 36 × 20 = 73.3.
(b) The top 10% start at the 90th percentile = 108th value: 80 + (108 − 102) ÷ 18 × 20 = 86.7. A student needs about 87 marks.
(c) The first group's median (57.1) is higher than the second class's (51), so the first group generally did better. The first group's IQR (73.3 − 42.9 = 30.4) is larger than 22, so its marks were more spread out (less consistent).
questions.tip: For the top 10% you need the 90th percentile, not the 10th.

questions.q:
Two box plots summarise the journey times, in minutes, for a commuter using Route A and Route B over many days.

          Min   Q₁   Median   Q₃   Max
Route A   18    24     27     35    52
Route B   20    23     29     31    38

(a) Describe the skewness of each distribution. Give reasons. [2]
(b) Determine whether the maximum time for Route A is an outlier, using the 1.5 × IQR rule. [2]
(c) The commuter must arrive at work within 35 minutes. Which route should she use? Give a reason based on the figures. [2]
ms: (a) B1: Route A positive skew because Q₃ − Q₂ = 8 > Q₂ − Q₁ = 3
(a) B1: Route B negative skew because Q₃ − Q₂ = 2 < Q₂ − Q₁ = 6

(c) B1: reason with figures, e.g. B's upper quartile (31) is below 35 so more than 75% of journeys are within 35 min, whereas for A only 75% are; or B's maximum (38) is lower than A's (52) / B less spread out (IQR 8 v 11)
questions.model:
(a) Route A: Q₃ − Q₂ = 8 and Q₂ − Q₁ = 3; 8 > 3 so positive skew.
Route B: Q₃ − Q₂ = 2 and Q₂ − Q₁ = 6; 2 < 6 so negative skew.
(b) IQR for A = 35 − 24 = 11. Upper limit = 35 + 16.5 = 51.5. Since 52 > 51.5, the maximum of 52 minutes is an outlier.
(c) Route B. Its upper quartile is 31 minutes, so more than 75% of journeys take under 35 minutes, compared with exactly 75% for Route A. Route B is also more consistent (IQR 8 v 11) and its longest journey is only 38 minutes, compared with 52 minutes for A, even though A has a slightly lower median.
questions.tip: A decision question needs a choice plus a reason quoting numbers from both routes.
